It locks strongly (1.1-2.0 of max) when the anchor is a digit numeral (years like 1932, numbers like 273, 42, 841) or a concrete or technical noun/subword (cigarette, smoke, virus, mitochondria, engine, non-Latin script pieces); it locks weakly (0.6-1.1) on everyday concrete nouns and activity words (dog, apple, milk, dinner, play), so about half of plain prose is active-weak; it stays at 0 across clauses made only of pronouns, person nouns (man, king, doctor, friend), abstract nouns (plan, idea, time, journey, epistemology) and spelled-out numbers (seven, nine).
